Why go: the island's sights by 4x4, with time for the elephants

This tour packs the classic Koh Samui sights into one day and adds what many families want most: time with elephants that does not involve riding them. The morning covers the south-east coast and the interior: the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rock formations, the mummified monk at Wat Khunaram, a swim at the first Na Muang waterfall and a coconut plantation. The 4x4 then leaves the tarmac for a track up to a high viewpoint and Wat Teepangkorn before lunch.

The afternoon is spent at an elephant camp, where you chop fruit and vegetables and roll sticky rice balls, then feed them to the elephants by hand.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: families and first-time visitors who want the main sights and an elephant encounter without organising transport.
  • Choose something else if you want a strictly observation-only sanctuary: this is an elephant camp, not a rescue sanctuary. Our elephant sanctuary guide explains the difference.
  • Not ideal for anyone with back problems: the hill tracks are rough in an open 4x4.

Good to know

  • Ethics: the tour includes no riding, no bathing and no shows. Keep your hands flat when feeding and follow the keepers' instructions; elephants are strong and can move suddenly.
  • Temples: cover shoulders and knees at Wat Khunaram and Wat Teepangkorn. A sarong in your bag solves it.
  • Waterfall: Na Muang 1 is a short walk from the car park. The rocks are slippery; wear sandals with grip.
  • Weather: November is Samui's wettest month. The day still runs, but bring a light rain jacket.
